xenogeneic.m: Denoting or relating to cells or tissues from individuals belonging to different species.

xenogenesis.m: The alternation of two or more different forms in the life cycle of a plant or animal.

xenograft.m: Tissue from an animal of one species used as a temporary graft (as in cases of severe burns) on an individual of another species.

xenografts.m: Tissue from an animal of one species used as a temporary graft (as in cases of severe burns) on an individual of another species.

xenolith.m: A piece of rock of different origin from the igneous rock in which it is embedded.

xenoliths.m: A piece of rock of different origin from the igneous rock in which it is embedded.

xenon.m: A colourless odourless inert gaseous element occurring in the earth's atmosphere in trace amounts.

xenophobia.m: A fear of foreigners or strangers.

xenophobic.m: Suffering from xenophobia; having abnormal fear or hatred of the strange or foreign.

xenotransplant.m: A surgical procedure in which tissue or whole organs are transfered from one species to another species.

xenotransplantation.m: A surgical procedure in which tissue or whole organs are transfered from one species to another species.

xenotransplantations.m: A surgical procedure in which tissue or whole organs are transfered from one species to another species.

xenotransplants.m: A surgical procedure in which tissue or whole organs are transfered from one species to another species.

xeroderma.m: A mild form of ichthyosis characterised by abnormal dryness and roughness of the skin.

xerodermas.m: A mild form of ichthyosis characterised by abnormal dryness and roughness of the skin.

xerodermia.m: A mild form of ichthyosis characterised by abnormal dryness and roughness of the skin.

xerodermias.m: A mild form of ichthyosis characterised by abnormal dryness and roughness of the skin.

xerography.e: Edge enhancement is intrinsic in xerography.
xerography.m: Forming an image by the action of light on a specially coated charged plate; the latent image is developed with powders that adhere only to electrically charged areas.

xerophile.m: Plant adapted for life with a limited supply of water; compare hydrophyte and mesophyte.

xerophthalmia.m: Abnormal dryness of the conjunctiva and cornea of the eyes; may be due to a systemic deficiency of vitamin A.

xerophthalmias.m: Abnormal dryness of the conjunctiva and cornea of the eyes; may be due to a systemic deficiency of vitamin A.

xerophyte.m: Plant adapted for life with a limited supply of water; compare hydrophyte and mesophyte.

xerophytes.m: Plant adapted for life with a limited supply of water; compare hydrophyte and mesophyte.

xerophytic.m: Adapted to a xeric (or dry) environment.

xeroradiographies.m: Radiography using X-rays and xerographic (rather than roentgenographic) techniques.

xeroradiography.m: Radiography using X-rays and xerographic (rather than roentgenographic) techniques.

xerostomia.m: Abnormal dryness of the mouth resulting from decreased secretion of saliva.

xerostomias.m: Abnormal dryness of the mouth resulting from decreased secretion of saliva.

xerox.m: A copy made by a xerographic copier.

xeroxes.m: A copy made by a xerographic copier.
